title: Tech View cells show a blue number, a thin progress bar and the advisor's avatar
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design picture "DC-05-tech-view-rows-regular-light-1440.png" attached to this case is open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and rank numbers in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two technicians are active at {Location-A} with the "Technician" role: {Technician-A}, who has a profile photo, and {Technician-B}, who has none.
    For example: {Technician-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Eva and {Technician-B} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Finn.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an Approved work order {Work-order-1}, led by {Technician-A}, with a service advisor and one approved line {Line-1} whose technician is {Technician-B}, who is clocked in to it; and an Invoiced work order {Work-order-2}, led by {Technician-A}.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST C590114 Cell Styles, {Work-order-1} and {Work-order-2} are S10043-17812 and S10043-17813, and {Line-1} is "Service - Full grease service".
  • Starting screen: "Work Orders" > "All" tab, "Tech View" shown, the name of {Customer-A} in "Search", no filter chosen, "Assigned to me" off, density "Regular".
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Look at the "Number" cell of the row for {Work-order-1}.
  2. Look at the "Progress" cell of the same row.
  3. Look at where the "Status", "Waiting On Parts" and "Progress" cells sit in their columns.
  4. Look at the "Service Advisor" cell.
  5. Look at the "Assigned Techs" cell.
  6. Hover the first avatar in the "Assigned Techs" cell.
  7. Look at the "Waiting On Parts", "Clocked In" and "Total price" cells.
  8. Look at the "Number" cell of the row for {Work-order-2}.
  9. Hover the small padlock next to that number.
  10. Click "List" in the display switcher.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the number is blue like a link, a little darker than the blue numbers in the design picture, not black.
  • Step 2: a thin rounded bar with the percentage beside it in small grey text (such as 0%), about as long as the word "Progress" in the header, as in the picture.
  • Step 3: all three sit at the left of their columns.
  • Step 4: a small round avatar sits before the advisor's name.
  • Step 5: overlapping round avatars, {Technician-A} (the lead) first, then {Technician-B}.
  • Step 6: a name bubble with {Technician-A}'s name opens above the avatar.
  • Step 7: "Waiting On Parts" shows a grey dash (-), not a blank, and "Total price" sits at the right of its column.
  • Step 8: a small padlock outline icon sits right after the number.
  • Step 9: a dark tooltip with light text opens above the padlock.
  • Step 10: List's "Clocked In" cell shows the same thing in the same style as Tech View's at step 7.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; stories SV-10045 (Story 2, Tech View), SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options), SV-10050 (Story 7, Line technicians); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 61 (16 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S2-R20, S2-R23, S1-R9a, S2-R8, S7-R3 and S7-R6, read 16 Oct 2026. Claude Design project "Work Orders" (Branko Cicovic), export of 14 Oct 2026, board "Work Orders.dc.html" (the design pictures named in the preconditions were rendered from it), read 14 Oct 2026. Related tickets: SV-11319, SV-11325. Product owner answers: Chris Ward, WO Board and Tech View question sheet (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1gBGmNB4B1bRrD2ZJvBn1tuvbfxFPjcsKddz_I5H3CvU), answer 31, read 15 Oct 2026. Source-verified 16 October 2026. Last checked against build v26.40.17-a5c4210 (staging) on 10/15/2026, before the expected results changed on 16 Oct 2026; the changed results have not yet been checked against a build.

The design shows Clocked In as a time badge (for example 0:48); this case follows the PRD, which keeps List's display (PRD version 51 onwards; Chris Ward confirmed on 15 Oct 2026, answer 31, that the names show as the List shows them). The design also locks Declined and Imported work orders; this case checks the padlock on an Invoiced one only.

PRD version 55 (S2-R20; Chris Ward ruling on Slavcho Mitrov's questions, 15 Oct 2026) sets the number link to the design system's link colour #175CD3, which meets accessible contrast; the design file's lighter blue does not, so step 1 expects a slightly darker blue than the picture. Versions 55 and 60 (S2-R23) also left-align Status, Waiting On Parts and Progress and open a row avatar's name bubble above it. Clicking the number to open the work order is checked in C96932.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R20: “Tech View’s cells follow the design: the work order number shows as a link in the design system’s link color (#175CD3), which meets accessible contrast on white; Progress shows as a thin bar with the percentage beside it, with no hours line under it at any density (S6-R6); Service Advisor shows the advisor’s avatar before the name. Clocked In keeps List’s display (S5-R11).”
  • S2-R23: “In Tech View and Board View, as in the design: a technician avatar without a photo is a light-grey circle (--sv-grey-100, #EEF2F6) with initials in --sv-grey-600 (#4B5565) in light mode, which meets accessible contrast (6.7:1; the design file’s #697586 is 4.2:1); dark mode uses the design’s dark colors; group and column header names are 14px, weight 600, in the design’s slate text color (#364152), with the design’s smaller, lighter initials; Board card customer and total price are weight 500; toolbar and switcher icons are the design’s slate color (the switcher in List too, S1-R9a). Technician avatars, and the Service Advisor avatar, follow density in Tech View as in the design: 20px, 24px and 32px on rows and 24px, 28px and 36px on group headers at Compact, Regular and Comfortable; Board View card avatars stay 24px. The Progress bar is 48 by 4px at Compact, as in the design. The name bubble on hover over a technician avatar on a row or card (the +N included) opens above the avatar, in both views; group and column header avatars keep the browser’s plain name tip, because the name is printed beside them. In Tech View, Status, Waiting On Parts and Progress are left-aligned. The Density and Columns tooltips open above their button, like the switcher’s (S1-R9b), and are hidden while their menu is open. List is unchanged.”
  • S1-R9a: “The switcher uses the design’s icons at 20px: List is Lucide `list`, Tech View is `user-round`, Board View is `square-kanban`. In Tech View and Board View these icons are the design’s: density (`row-height` in Tech View, `card-height` in Board View, custom icons in the design system’s icon set), collapse chevron (`chevron-down`), pin and unpin (`pin` / `pin-off`), Invoiced or Paid lock (`lock`), Unassigned avatar (`user-round`) and the empty state when there are no work orders at all (`clipboard-list`). The filtered no-results state is the List’s, magnifier included (S1-N1). The filter chips and Search use the design file’s icons in every display option, List included, each exactly as the design file draws it. The display switcher (new on every view, List included) shows the design’s slate icons in every view, so it keeps one color as the user moves between views. These are the only changes to List. Every other List icon is unchanged.”
  • S2-R8: “Clicking anywhere on a row, outside its own controls, opens the work order. A drag starts only after the pointer has moved a few pixels, so a click never turns into a drag.”
  • S7-R3: “Place the lead technician first in the avatar group.”
  • S7-R6: “Keep every involved technician discoverable by name.”
